scope: R190: where the 6.00 us per FA tile actually goes - not compute, not bandwidth, not softmax

softmax_ruled_out.conclusion: even at 12 vector ops per element softmax uses at most 21% of the vector peak, so it is not the bottleneck

hbm_ruled_out.conclusion: HBM sits at 23%, so bandwidth is not the limiter either

conclusion.evidence: cube 24%, vector at most 21%, HBM 23% - all three units idle most of the time is the signature of a lack of overlap
contributing_factors: the per-tile QK^T -> softmax -> PV chain has to complete serially with insufficient double buffering to hide MTE and vector work behind cube work
Bc=304 is not a multiple of 128, so cube work on the K dimension fragments into 2x128+48
829 waves across 30 cores means any fixed per-wave synchronisation cost is paid 829 times

implications.optimisation_direction: overlap and pipelining, not fewer ops; fusing maths would bring little

directions.name: double buffering / deeper pipeline
directions.reason: most likely, given all three units sit near 20%

directions.name: align Bc to a multiple of 128
directions.reason: 304 = 2x128+48, so the last 48 columns must run cube inefficiently

directions.name: fewer waves / more work per core
directions.reason: amortise any fixed per-wave cost across 829 waves

implications.for_10s: R189 showed only 1.50x is needed; this round says that 1.50x comes from removing bubbles rather than doing more, and bubbles are 76% of the tile, so removing a third of them suffices

not_measured: all of the above is arithmetic inference; the bubble hypothesis needs occupancy traces
next_steps: capture AICore and vector occupancy of the FA kernel with msprof or the torch_npu profiler and check whether the two units do not overlap
sweep Bc over 128/256/304/384 to test the cube-fragmentation hypothesis
both are cheap and change no maths; a tile change alters accumulation order so it is numerically non-equivalent and would be measurement only, never a candidate without approval
